:::{#exm-poisson-sufficient}
#### The sum is sufficient for a Poisson rate

Let $\dsn{X} \siid \Pois(\rate)$ and $S \eqdef \sumin \Rvar_\iobs$.
The joint mass function of the sample is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\pdf\paren{\vx ; \rate}
&= \prod_{i=1}^n \frac{e^{-\rate} \rate^{\rvar_\iobs}}{\rvar_\iobs!}
&& \text{(independent Poisson mass functions)}\\
&= e^{-n\rate} \rate^{\sumin \rvar_\iobs} \prod_{i=1}^n \frac{1}{\rvar_\iobs!}
&& \text{(collect the factors)}
\end{aligned}
$$

This has the form of @eq-factorization with
$\sfacf{t}{\rate} = e^{-n\rate} \rate^{t}$ and $\rfacf{\vx} = \prod_{i=1}^n 1 / \rvar_\iobs!$,
where $t = \sumin \rvar_\iobs$.
So the sum $S$ is [sufficient](#def-sufficient) for $\rate$ by @thm-factorization.
:::
